reason: The hypothesis relies on RTA inducing ordering or anisotropic distortions to boost coercivity in FeCoNi-based HEAs. E1 shows a 40-fold coercivity increase in RTA-treated FeCoNiMnCu without Pt, and E2 attributes this to anisotropic strain or directional chemical order, directly supporting the mechanism. E1 also demonstrates L10 ordering with Pt addition, but the hypothesis proposes L10 ordering in a Pt-free FeCoNi system, which is not supported by the cited evidence and overstates the findings.
premises: RTA of FeCoNiMnCu thin films increases coercivity ~40-fold without Pt
RTA-induced coercivity increase arises from anisotropic strain, lattice distortions, or directional chemical order
RTA can stabilize L10 ordering in FeCoNi-based HEAs when Pt is present
The coercivity enhancement mechanism is distinct from dewetting or secondary phase effects
